Microsoft just revealed it built an 8-trillion-parameter AI model entirely in-house — no distillation from OpenAI or anyone else.

This is a big deal. For three years, Microsoft was the money behind OpenAI. Now it has its own frontier model that reportedly outperforms the base behind GPT 5.6 Soul, and it has not even gone through reinforcement learning yet.

The architecture uses mixture-of-experts with 80 billion active parameters — comparable in design to other leading models at this scale. What matters for business leaders is not the parameter count. It is what this signals about where the AI industry is heading.

The frontier model layer is consolidating around a handful of companies with the compute budgets to train at this level. Microsoft, Google, Anthropic, Meta — that is increasingly the full list. For everyone else, the competitive advantage shifts from which model you use to how fast and effectively you deploy AI across your operations.

If you are a CTO managing vendor relationships, this changes the calculus on lock-in. If you are a CEO setting AI strategy, the question becomes: when model quality converges, what makes your AI investment defensible?
